questions.question: Your body removes alcohol at what rate?

options.text: About one drink per hour.
About two drinks per hour.
About three drinks per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: About one drink per hour.
questions.explanation: Your body removes about one drink of alcohol per hour. This can vary from person to person. The safest choice is to not ride after drinking any alcohol.

questions.question: Is texting and driving allowed?

options.text: No, it is illegal.
Yes, when stopped at traffic lights.
Yes, when there is light traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, it is illegal.
questions.explanation: Texting while driving is very dangerous. It increases crash risk by up to 23 times. South Dakota law makes texting while driving illegal.

questions.question: What should you do when riding at night?

options.text: Ride at the same speed as daytime.
Ride slower than daytime.
Ride faster than daytime.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride slower than daytime.
questions.explanation: Ride slower at night, especially on roads you don't know. Going slower gives you more time to spot and avoid hazards when it's dark.

questions.question: Where do most conflicts happen between motorcycles and other vehicles?

options.text: At intersections
On highways
On any road

questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections
questions.explanation: Intersections are where conflicts between motorcycles and other vehicles happen most often.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT help reduce serious injury in a crash?

options.text: A DOT-approved helmet.
A leather jacket.
A sweatshirt.

questions.correctAnswerText: A sweatshirt.
questions.explanation: A DOT-approved helmet protects your head and neck in a crash. A leather or sturdy synthetic jacket also provides protection. A sweatshirt does not.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slippery when wet
Lanes shift
Yield

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns that the road ahead may be slippery when wet.

questions.question: If hazards are to your right, which side of your lane should you ride on?

options.text: Right side
Left side
Either side

questions.correctAnswerText: Left side
questions.explanation: Position yourself to have the most space. If hazards are on your right, ride on the left side of your lane. If hazards are on your left, ride on the right side.

questions.question: What should you do when changing lanes?

options.text: Your mirrors show you everything you need to see.
Turn your head to check your blind spot in addition to using mirrors.
Signal and immediately move left or right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head to check your blind spot in addition to using mirrors.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any vehicle. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes, even after checking your mirrors.

questions.question: What is true about motorcycle mirrors?

options.text: They show everything perfectly.
They do not show blind spots.
You should only use them when parking.

questions.correctAnswerText: They do not show blind spots.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle mirrors have blind spots like any vehicle. Always turn your head to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: When riding near a truck, what should you remember?

options.text: If you cannot see the truck's mirrors, the driver cannot see you.
You should not be able to see the truck's mirrors.
Focus on operating your motorcycle and ignore the truck's mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you cannot see the truck's mirrors, the driver cannot see you.
questions.explanation: Stay out of large trucks' blind spots. If you can't see the truck's mirrors, the driver can't see you either.

questions.question: If another vehicle is passing you, where should you ride?

options.text: In the left part of the lane.
In the center of the lane.
In the right part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, ride in the center of the lane. This is the safest position. Riding near the passing vehicle increases the risk of a collision. Riding on the far side may make the driver return to your lane too quickly and unsafely.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Make it easier for others to see you.
Help you avoid road hazards.
Invite other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Invite other drivers to share your lane.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you be seen, avoid hazards and blind spots, and keeps other drivers out of your lane. It also gives you an escape route if danger appears. Your position should NOT invite other drivers to share your lane.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Protects your face only, not your eyes.
Protects your eyes only, not your whole face.
Protects your whole face.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protects your whole face.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield gives full protection to your face and eyes in a crash. A windshield alone is not enough protection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield
Slow-moving vehicle
Railroad crossing

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle
questions.explanation: This sign is placed on the back of slow-moving vehicles that travel below 25 mph. Examples include construction equipment, farm machinery, and horse-drawn vehicles.

questions.question: Taking over-the-counter medicine before riding:

options.text: Is usually fine because over-the-counter drugs are weak.
Is always safe.
May harm your riding ability and needs careful thought.

questions.correctAnswerText: May harm your riding ability and needs careful thought.
questions.explanation: Many drugs, including over-the-counter and prescription medicines, can affect your ability to ride safely. Talk to your doctor about how any new medicine may affect your driving or riding.

questions.question: If a driver makes eye contact with you:

options.text: You know they have seen you.
It does not always mean they have actually seen you.
They will give you the right of way.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not always mean they have actually seen you.
questions.explanation: Never assume a driver has seen you just because they looked at you. A driver may look directly at you and still fail to actually notice you.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, where should you ride?

options.text: In the left part of the lane.
In the center of the lane.
In the right part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, ride in the center of your lane. This is usually the safest position. Riding near the passing driver risks a collision. Riding on the far side may cause the driver to return to your lane too soon.

questions.question: The best way to stop quickly is to:

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use the rear brake before the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Always use the front and rear brakes together when making a quick stop.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks up while stopping on good pavement, you should:

options.text: Keep the wheel locked until you fully stop.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake and quickly apply it again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the wheel locked until you fully stop.
questions.explanation: If you lock the rear wheel on good pavement while stopping, keep it locked until you stop completely. You can still control your motorcycle if it is upright and going straight, even with a locked rear wheel.

questions.question: A solid white line on the edge of the road means:

options.text: No parking allowed.
The right edge of the traffic lane.
Traffic must merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right edge of the traffic lane.
questions.explanation: A solid white line on the edge of the road marks the right edge of the traffic lane.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid danger, what should you do?

options.text: Use only the front brake while swerving.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Brake first, then swerve, or swerve first, then brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake first, then swerve, or swerve first, then brake.
questions.explanation: Do these actions separately, not at the same time. Braking while swerving can cause your motorcycle to tip over.

questions.question: When scanning the area around your motorcycle, what should you look for?

options.text: Escape routes near intersections, shopping areas, and schools.
Opportunities to travel faster than other vehicles.
Pedestrians to watch closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Escape routes near intersections, shopping areas, and schools.
questions.explanation: Look for escape routes at intersections, shopping areas, schools, and construction zones. This helps you avoid hazards.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Come to a complete stop.
Proceed through the intersection with caution.
Yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red traffic light. You must stop completely and wait for a signal that allows you to turn in your direction.

questions.question: How should a group of motorcyclists pass another vehicle?

options.text: In a staggered formation.
In pairs.
One at a time.

questions.correctAnswerText: One at a time.
questions.explanation: On a two-lane road, pass one motorcycle at a time. Each rider must finish passing before the next rider begins.

questions.question: What should you wear when riding during the day?

options.text: Clothing with reflective material.
A short-sleeved shirt.
Dark-colored clothing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Clothing with reflective material.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear reflective clothing so other drivers can see you better. Always wear clothing that covers your arms and legs.
